text:
Mavrik Bourque spent his whole pro career in the Dallas organization before this season: drafted 30th overall by the Stars in 2020, then 47 points for their AHL affiliate in Texas. On Wednesday he came back to American Airlines Center in a Nashville sweater and scored the goal that held up for most of the night, a wrist shot with 58 seconds left in the first period, off Brady Skjei and Ryan O'Reilly. That put the Predators' win chance at 65%, and Dallas never got even.

This was a goaltenders' game for long stretches, and both were good. Jake Oettinger, who already has a league-best five shutouts, stopped 24 of 25 and saved about 1.5 goals more than the chances deserved. Juuse Saros was the more valuable of the two by our wins-added measure: 20 saves on 21 shots, including the biggest stop of the night on Roope Hintz with a little under six minutes to play and the Stars pressing for a tie.

The underlying game leaned Nashville's way, more than the 1-0 score through 58 minutes suggested. The Predators dominated the second period, 1.26 expected goals (our measure of chance quality) to Dallas's 0.14, and finished with 3.84 to 1.76 overall. By our replays of every shot, they deserved to win 64% of the time. O'Reilly, whose name has been floating around trade chatter this month, was on the ice for 1.78 expected goals for and only 0.33 against, with two assists.

The finish was frantic. Ross Colton scored the winner with 1:21 left, a 55% chance set up by Filip Forsberg and Jayden Struble. Wyatt Johnston answered for Dallas 46 seconds later off Tyler Seguin, and Jack Drury put it away into the empty net with 15 seconds to go. That ended the Stars' five-game winning streak, a run that included Jamie Benn reaching 1,000 career points. Nashville has now beaten Dallas twice this season, both times by playing a tighter game than the Stars wanted.
headline: Bourque scores on his old team as Predators end Stars' run
